intent_snapshot.goal: Carry a refuted Review finding forward with its executable counterevidence so a later independent Review round does not rediscover it as new work, while the refutation loses force the moment its bound evidence goes stale.

acceptance.assertion: parseAssuranceVerdict rejects a review-role rework verdict whose findings omit evidence.trigger, a non-empty evidence.caller_chain, or evidence.violated {kind, ref}, returning the existing verdict_invalid blocked result without writing authority; a complete verdict parses and derives a stable sha256 anchor over the canonical {violated.kind, violated.ref, caller_chain}; QA-role and pass verdicts are unchanged; and buildReviewPrompt instructs the required evidence fields without disclosing any prior finding.

A refute_finding operation and action set an open finding to status refuted with a counterevidence binding of {attestation_id, acceptance_id}, and are rejected with a KernelInvariantError when no fresh passing QA attestation in the record covers that acceptance_id; TaskFinding gains only optional anchor and counterevidence fields so the TaskRecord contract is not bumped, and the append-only invariant still rejects finding removal and any rewrite other than the open-to-resolved and open-to-refuted transitions.

request_rework records a new review finding whose anchor matches a live refuted finding as status refuted with that finding's inherited counterevidence binding, so it is not counted in blocking_finding_ids while the bound attestation stays fresh, and records a review finding carrying a different anchor as status open so it still blocks completion; findingsDigestV2 covers anchor so a capability minted for one anchor set cannot be spent on another.

Refutation liveness is derived rather than stored: completionDecision counts a refuted finding as blocking again as soon as its bound attestation leaves the fresh set because diff_hash or the intent revision changed, and projectTask then reports next_obligation resolve_findings, while a refuted finding whose attestation is still fresh neither blocks completion nor appears in blocking_finding_ids.

The replan boundary parks a task only when a new blocking review finding that was not admitted as refuted shares an acceptance boundary with a prior blocking review finding, where a shared boundary means an equal acceptance_id or, when both are null, an equal evidence.violated.ref; a second-round blocking review finding on an unrelated acceptance boundary no longer writes a replan_required finding.

The Claude and Pi host adapters both forward evidence and anchor from the parsed verdict into the findings array they pass to findingsDigestV2 when minting the request_rework capability, so the two hosts produce the same findings digest for the same verdict and neither can submit review findings that reach the Kernel without an anchor.

The code-review role prompt states the required finding evidence fields and their anchor semantics, and the checked-in generated mirror under plugins/immune-brain/dist/role-prompts/ matches its runtime source so the packaged reviewer contract cannot drift from the runtime one.
